title: fix(post): G76 words state the thread passes that were verified
body:
**Replaces #433** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #432 (#416).** Part of #363.

## What changed
**With the G76 cycle post option, the G76 words now describe the passes the verdict judged.** G32 passes stay the default output.
- The record maps 1:1: `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)` / `G76 X Z P(k) Q(dd) F`, where:
  - dd = the first pass's depth;
  - dmin = the step (constant depth) or the plan's minimum (constant area);
  - d = the finishing pass's own depth;
  - m = 1 + spring passes;
  - a = twice the flank angle.
- **Control model** (GSK988TA, Fanuc-compatible G76):
  - each roughing pass goes to `max(dd·√n, previous + dmin)`, up to k − d;
  - the first finishing pass cuts d, and m − 1 more repeat at k;
  - each pass starts `depth·tan(a/2)` along Z.
- **Refused by name with G76 chosen:** alternating infeed (the CL carries a new `alternating` flag; `ALT 1` is written to the stream only when set), a doubled angle outside 0/29/30/55/60/80 (so 29.5° is refused), and a one-pass thread.

**⚠ This changes posted output for the default G76 thread: `R0` becomes `R0.4`.** The golden `fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` changes on one line: `G76 P010000 Q400 R0` → `G76 P010000 Q400 R0.4`.
- Why: with `R0` the control roughs 0.4, 0.8 and 1.2, then cuts its finishing pass at the root again. That is a fourth full-depth pass the verdict never judged. It is not a gouge, but it is not what was verified.
- With `R0.4` it roughs 0.4 and 0.8 and finishes at 1.2: the three passes we judge.
- Making `R0` true instead would have meant changing G32 output and the judged passes.
- Note: the #363 research said Q = infeed made the control cut a decreasing ladder. That is not so, because dmin = infeed clamps every step equal. The real gap was R.

**R comes from the rounded words' own ladder (M3 review fix, head 0bb37ddd).** The control reads the posted words, each rounded to the least increment on its own. In inch, `Q157 P472 R0.0157` left k − d = 0.0315 one increment past the second rung 0.0314, so the control cut a 4th, unverified pass. Now the post counts the record's rough passes N from its own ladder, rebuilds rungs N−1 and N from the rounded Q (first depth), Q (minimum depth) and P (thread height), and writes the R whose last rough depth P − R lies in (rung N−1, rung N], nearest the record's allowance. Inch golden: `R0.0158` (control: 0.0157 / 0.0314 / 0.0472). If that R is more than one least increment from the record's allowance, the cycle is refused by name (the Q/Q/P words and the R window are named). The other G76 words (X, Z, P k, Q dd, Q dmin) are each one record value rounded once, not differences, so R was the only derived word. The Tormach (LinuxCNC) G76 has the same class of gap in J/K (inch `J0.0314 K0.0944` = ceil 4 passes for a 3-pass record), filed as #1619. Its goldens are left byte-identical to main here.

**A project cached before this PR posts R0 until the op is regenerated.** Checked: the stale stamp (`crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs`, `current_stamp`) hashes only the operation's inputs (tool, params, source, heights). It has no generator version, and the cached record's `finish_allowance` reads back as saved (0). So such an op reads **Fresh**, not Stale:
- The Fanuc post writes `R0` for it: the output of main before this PR (one extra root pass in mm), not a gouge.
- The Tormach post refuses it by name, because it expects the ladder's last step. That is safe, but the message does not tell the user to regenerate the operation. Follow-up: #1843 (P7).

`docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`

## How tested
- New app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` (4 tests):
  - a new flank, constant-area golden `thread_g76_area.nc` (`G76 P020055 Q100 R0.05` / `G76 X9.6 Z14 P1200 Q400 F2`): the control's schedule computed from the posted words matches the laid depths and stations within 1 µm (under the readings that the post uses; see "Not proven" below);
  - the default (`R0.4`) and a 0.5 step (`Q500 R0.2`) also match;
  - one refusal per unexpressible option;
  - `ALT` survives the stream and the project file.
- M3 review fix (head 0bb37ddd), two new tests in `lathe_post_g76_schedule`:
  - `the_default_thread_g76_states_its_three_passes_in_inch`: posts the default thread under G20, parses the G76 words, runs the control's ladder on them, and asserts exactly 3 passes matching the laid depths (`R0.0158`).
  - `a_ladder_the_rounded_words_cannot_state_is_refused_by_name`: two hand-edited inch records (13 and 39 sqrt rungs, 2 and 4 increments off) are refused by name, and the same record in mm posts.
  - Mutations, each red and then reverted: R back to `fu(finish)` (inch twin + refusal test); refusal dropped (refusal test); check `> 2` (refusal test, 2-increment case); check `> 0` / `>= 1` (inch twin + refusal test).
  - Gate: app lathe_post_g76 8, lathe_post_g76_schedule 6, lathe_post_inch 6, lathe_post 7, lathe_post_tormach 8, lathe_post_tormach_thread 8, tormach_lathes 2, recorded_post_streams 5; post lathe_post_refusals 11, script_fanuc_lathe 15; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean. Tormach lathe goldens: `git diff upstream/main` empty.
- Existing post, cl, inverted_post, lathe_post, golden_cl, project_roundtrip, tool_law, tool_gate and commands_undo suites are green.
- (Superseded.) Takeover refresh at 49d0a3c2: merged upstream/main cleanly, and set the inch golden to `R0.0157`. The M3 review fix at 0bb37ddd replaced that value with `R0.0158`. The head writes `R0.0158`.
- Takeover by the owner account (2026-11-15, maintainer's order), head be4546ca: merged origin/main db091cb3 with no conflicts. `git diff origin/main --stat` lists only this PR's 20 files. The inch golden stays `R0.0158`. Gate: cl and post batch steps green; motion lib 366, turning_thread 18, turning_thread_cycle 3, turning_thread_infeed 8; app lib 313, lathe_post 7, lathe_post_g76 8, lathe_post_g76_schedule 6, lathe_post_inch 6, lathe_post_css 10, lathe_post_tormach 8, lathe_post_tormach_g30 4, lathe_post_tormach_thread 8, lathe_thread_travel 2, lathe_field_tools 2, lathe_cycle_exit 6, lathe_work_spindle 5, tormach_lathes 2, turning_thread 10, turning_thread_infeed 4, thread_passes 5, recorded_post_streams 5, golden_cl 33, project_roundtrip 73, posting 17, conformance 7, coarse_laws 6, program_units 7, post_unit_word 5; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. Not run: sim, geometry, kernel, tools and ui suites (not touched).
- Head 5c23149d (answer to the full review of be4546ca): text only. It changes `docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md` and no code, test or golden. No gate was run for it.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` (cl, post, motion, app, ui) is clean.
- The gate escalated to batch (cl changed). It fails only on tests already red on main: headless GPU, #415, and `swarf_pose_continuity` (PR #351).

## Not proven: four Fanuc G76 readings (no Fanuc control run exists)
No source that we read states these readings, and no run on a Fanuc control or simulator confirms them. In the list, k is the thread height and a the tool angle (twice the flank angle).
1. **Z-shift sign, and which pass sits at the programmed Z.** The post follows LinuxCNC's sign and sets the start Z to `c_first - k·tan(a/2)`. If the control shifts the other way, or its finishing pass sits at the programmed start Z, the whole thread moves axially by `k·tan(a/2)` to `2k·tan(a/2)` (0.6 to 1.25 mm for `thread_g76_area.nc`, 2 mm lead). That is a cut in the wrong place.
2. **End-Z shift.** If the control also shifts the end of each pass by `depth·tan(a/2)`, the root pass ends `k·tan(a/2)` past the programmed end Z. At a shoulder, that can cut into the shoulder.
3. **Minimum-depth clamp reading** (read as a per-pass minimum, per the manual's definition). A different reading changes the pass count or the per-pass depth only, never the root. It can give fewer, deeper passes than verified (the tool load is not judged). Equal-depth ladders (the default) are not affected.
4. **Rounding.** The pass count is fixed by construction (R from the rounded ladder, refused beyond one increment). Single rungs of a long sqrt ladder can still differ from the laid ones by a few increments. That is not a gouge.

Items 1 and 2 can move a flank thread (a ≠ 0) axially, or into a shoulder. They stay unproven without a Fanuc control run. The default radial thread (a = 0) has no Z shift, so items 1 and 2 do not change it. Main already carries the risk of items 1 and 2 for flank threads (#416 posts the angle and the start); this PR does not add it. Items 3 and 4 do not move the cut. The Fanuc run (or a refusal or warning for a flank G76 until the run) is tracked in #1842.

The PathPilot Hub simulation cannot check items 1-4: its lathe is LinuxCNC's one-block G76, not Fanuc's two-block G76. A Hub run is not needed for the Tormach side: the Tormach lathe goldens are byte-identical to main (checked against upstream/main). Only Fanuc-lathe goldens change (`thread_g76.nc` mm and inch, new `thread_g76_area.nc`). The inch Fanuc golden reads `R0.0158`.

Changelog: G76 threading output states the passes that were verified: the finish allowance R is posted (default threads now post R0.4 instead of R0), and options G76 cannot express are refused by name (#417)

Fixes #417
